title: Should You Get Back Together With Your Ex? A Decision Guide — cv.cm
description: Should you get back together with your ex? Questions to ask yourself, good and bad reasons to try again, what must change first, and how to restart slowly.
h1: Should you get back together with your ex?
answer: Get back together only if the reason you broke up has really changed, both of you want to try for reasons other than loneliness, and you can talk about the old problems calmly. If it ended because of abuse, control or repeated cheating, or if you have already broken up and returned many times without change, a second try is unlikely to be different.

sections.h: The one question that matters most
body: Getting back together has many names: 复合 in Chinese, 復縁 in Japanese, 재결합 in Korean, volver con tu ex in Spanish. The feelings are similar everywhere. You miss the person, the routine and the future you planned. Those feelings are real, but they do not tell you whether the relationship will work this time.

The most useful question is simple: what is different now? If the honest answer is "we miss each other", nothing has changed yet. If the answer is "the distance is over", "I have been in counselling for my temper for four months", or "we both now want to live in the same city", there may be something to build on.
This page is for deciding. If you already decided you want to try and want to know how to reach out honestly, see cv.cm's guide on how to get your ex back.

sections.h: Questions to ask yourself before you decide
body: Answer these in writing, alone, on a calm day. Then, if it helps, talk them through with a friend who knows you both and will be honest.

ol: Why did we break up, in one or two sentences that both of us would agree with?
Has that reason changed? What exactly is the evidence?
Who changed: one of us, or both? Is the change in actions, or only in promises?
Am I thinking of going back because I love this person, or because I am lonely, scared of starting over, or hurt that they moved on?
Do I feel safe with them, including when we disagree?
Do my friends and family, who saw the relationship, have serious concerns? Why?
If we broke up again in six months, what would the reason be?
Would I advise a close friend to go back to this relationship?

body: If you struggle to answer question 1 or question 2, you are not ready to decide yet. Give it more time.

sections.h: What has to change first, and what research says
body: Researchers who studied on-again/off-again dating relationships (Dailey and colleagues, 2009) found these couples reported fewer positives, such as love and understanding, and more negatives, such as communication problems and uncertainty, than couples who had not broken up. More breakups and renewals went with more negatives. The organization loveisrespect makes a similar point: couples can break up and reconcile successfully, but when breakups keep repeating, the relationship is not working well, and the odds of recovering go down.

The lesson is not "never go back". It is that going back to the same relationship gives the same result. Something has to change in how you treat each other. The Gottman Institute's research names four patterns that predict relationships ending: criticism, contempt, defensiveness and stonewalling. If these were common in your fights, the change you need is a new way to disagree, not more love.
Concrete changes that make a real difference:

ul: The practical cause is gone: the move, the job, the visa, the exam year.
The person who broke trust has been fully honest and accepts that trust returns slowly.
A habit that hurt the relationship has been addressed for months, often with professional help: drinking, gambling, anger, constant phone use, jealousy.
Both of you agree on the big life questions that split you: marriage, children, where to live.
Both of you, not just one, want to try and are willing to put effort in.

body: If you both decide to try, treat it as a new relationship with history, not a return to the old one.

ol: Talk about the old problems first. For example: "Before we start again, I want us to talk about why it ended. I think part of it was that I stopped telling you when something bothered me. What do you think it was?"
Agree on one or two new rules. For example: "If one of us needs space during a fight, we say when we will come back." Or: "We have a real date once a week."
Go slower than before. Do not move in together, announce it widely, or make big promises in the first weeks.
Keep your own life: your friends, hobbies and routines. Losing them may have been part of the problem.
Set a check-in. After about three months, ask each other honestly: "Is this better than before? What still feels the same?"
Consider couples counselling, especially after cheating or if the same fight keeps coming back.

sections.h: When to end it for good
body: Some relationships should not get a second, third or fourth try. End it for good when:

ul: There has been violence, threats, or control over your money, phone, friends or movements.
Cheating or serious lying has happened more than once.
You have broken up and got back together several times and nothing has changed.
You only feel relief when you are apart.
One of you wants marriage or children and the other clearly does not.

body: Ending it for good does not mean the relationship had no value. It means you are choosing to stop the cycle. See cv.cm's guide on how to get over a breakup for the next steps.

body.note: If you feel afraid of an ex or partner, it is not your fault, and help exists. Contact local emergency services if you are in danger. A domestic violence helpline, such as loveisrespect.org or thehotline.org in the US, or a local service where you live, can help you think through your options.

faq.q: Is getting back with an ex a good idea?
faq.a: It can be, when the reason for the breakup has really changed and both people want to try. It is usually a poor idea when the main reasons are loneliness, jealousy or fear of starting over.

faq.q: Do couples who get back together last?
faq.a: Some do, especially after breakups caused by timing. Research on on-again/off-again couples suggests that, on average, repeated cycles go with more problems, so what changes between tries matters more than the decision to try.

faq.q: Should I get back together with someone who cheated?
faq.a: Only if they are fully honest, take responsibility without blaming you, and accept that trust will return slowly, often with counselling. If it has happened more than once, the pattern matters more than the apology.

faq.q: How long should you wait before getting back together?
faq.a: Long enough for both of you to calm down and for real change to show, often at least one to two months. Deciding in the first week after a breakup is usually driven by pain, not judgement.

faq.q: Can a relationship be better the second time?
faq.a: Yes, if both people learned something and changed how they act. A second try that repeats the same habits usually ends for the same reasons.
